If Δ > 0, you get two real solutions: x = [-b ± √Δ] / 2a. If Δ = 0, one real solution: x = -b/2a. If Δ < 0, two complex solutions. Check your work by plugging solutions back in. It's like following a baking recipe - precise measurements matter. Don't overcomplicate it.

First, find the derivative f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x - these are stationary points. Then find second derivative f''(x). For each stationary point, plug into f''(x): if positive, it's a minimum; if negative, maximum; if zero, test further. Finally, plug x-values into original f(x) to get y-coordinates. It's systematic like rock climbing - plan your route, execute carefully. Don't rush the calculations.
